name: NVIDIA Dynamo
license: Apache-2.0 (README badge and SPDX headers; GitHub's license API reports NOASSERTION because some bundled paths ship NVIDIA-proprietary components, e.g. NIXL's ucx IB modules)
notable_features: Orchestration layer ABOVE the inference engines - the README is explicit that it 'doesn't replace SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or vLLM, it turns them into a coordinated multi-node inference system'; backend support matrix lists all three for disaggregated serving
Disaggregated serving with independently scalable prefill and decode pools
KV-aware routing to avoid redundant prefill computation across replicas
SLA-based Planner for autoscaling against measured latency, and a profiler that derives cost models for disaggregated deployments (per-engine disagg templates for vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM)
KVBM block manager for GPU/host KV tiering - marked complete for TensorRT-LLM and vLLM, in progress for SGLang
KV transfer via NIXL (NixlConnector), Mooncake and LMCache connectors
Rust core with Python extensibility; frontend/worker split with graph-deployment CRDs for Kubernetes
hardware_caveats: NVIDIA-originated: the disaggregation and NIXL paths are built on CUDA/UCX, so the CUDA support is first-class and anything else is secondary
NIXL itself is Linux-only - 'macOS and Windows are not currently supported; use a Linux host or container/VM' - so the whole KV-transfer stack is Linux-only
NIXL was tested with UCX 1.23.x and needs GDRCopy for maximum RDMA performance (works without it, slower)
Multi-node disaggregated deployments require an RDMA-capable fabric; the known-failure cases in the tracker are all fabric-configuration failures rather than code failures
best_for: Multi-node production serving where prefill and decode need to be scaled and costed independently
Kubernetes-based deployments that want an OpenAI-compatible frontend, SLA-driven autoscaling and KV-aware routing as one stack
Fleets that already run vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM and want disaggregation without changing engine
avoid_for: Single-node or single-GPU serving, where the README itself says 'If you're running a single model on a single GPU, your inference engine alone is probably sufficient'
Non-Linux hosts - the NIXL dependency alone rules out Windows and macOS

Workloads that need bit-reproducible output across prefill and decode pools without extra configuration; the KV compatibility hash omits batch-invariance mode and some connectors have no model-level check at all
notes: KV transfer path: NIXL as the primary connector (NixlConnector), with UCX as the default transport and RDMA/GPUDirect for inter-node, plus Mooncake and LMCache as alternative connectors and KVBM for GPU/host tiering. UCX-specific env vars are required - the vLLM connector guide notes NCCL variables such as NCCL_IB_HCA do not apply to the NIXL path. Does Dynamo supersede or complement the Triton/TRT-LLM paths? Complement, and by design it does not try to replace them: it is an orchestration layer that drives them. The TRT-LLM maintainer response on issue #17665 is the clearest statement of the relationship - 'TensorRT-LLM disaggregated serving is now planned to fully adopt the Python transceiver', i.e. Dynamo supplies the runtime and TRT-LLM supplies the transceiver implementation. Handoff contract as implemented (components/src/dynamo/common/backend/disagg.py): prefill workers have max_tokens clamped to 1 because 'producing more than one token is wasted compute and breaks the prefill->decode handoff contract', and a decode-mode worker raises if the request arrives without a prefill_result, so a missing handoff is a hard error rather than a silent recompute. Its tracker also shows the operational surface is still young: open multi-node hang reports (#11914), a UCX_NET_DEVICES silent-garbage root cause (#12463, triaged urgent), an LMCache-on-vLLM silent cache corruption report (#14416), and an RFC to bind batch-invariance into KV namespaces (#58263 in vLLM). ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-04 (0 months), latest release v1.5.0 published 2026-09-21, 420 contributors, open_issues_count 1658 (issues PLUS pull requests), NOT archived, 8219 stars.
